content.text:
I fixed the bug: a link whose text contains another link now keeps its outer brackets as plain text, and only the inner link is rendered. Both examples from the report now give the CommonMark output: ``` [foo [bar](/uri)](/uri) →

[foo bar](/uri)

[foo [bar](/uri)][ref]\n\n[ref]: /uri →

[foo bar]ref

``` **Cause:** `outputLink` in `src/Tokenizer.ts` made a link out of every bracketed span it matched. It never checked whether the text inside already had a link. **Fix:** - **`src/Tokenizer.ts`:** after reading a link's text, `outputLink` now checks for a link at any depth, including inside emphasis or images. If it finds one, it returns a plain-text `[` instead, and the rest of the input is read normally, so the inner link wins. Images are never rejected this way, since the rule only applies to links. Because it can now return text, `link()`'s declared return type includes text, as `reflink()`'s already did. - **Same function, related fix:** it used to set the "inside a link" flag back to `false` after a nested link. That turned bare-URL autolinking back on for the rest of the outer link's text. It now restores the previous value. - **`src/Lexer.ts`:** when `link()` returns that `[` text, it is merged into the text before it, the same way the reflink branch already does. **Tests:** - Examples 518, 519 and 532 were marked as expected failures in two copies of the spec file (`test/specs/commonmark/` and `test/specs/gfm/`). I removed that mark in both. - I added a lexer test, "link inside link text", in `test/unit/Lexer.test.js`. - Spec tests: 1781 pass, 0 fail. Unit tests (Lexer, marked, Parser, Hooks, instance): 176 pass, 0 fail. - I couldn't run `tsc` or `eslint` because permission to run them was denied, so type-checking and lint are unchecked. The build with `node esbuild.config.js` succeeds. **Edge cases you might notice:** - `![[[foo](uri1)](uri2)](uri3)` (CommonMark example 520) is still wrong, as it was before. The image pattern can't match brackets nested that deeply. That's a separate, older limitation, and the test is still marked as an expected failure. - With GFM, a bare URL that ends a rejected outer link now gets autolinked and takes in the trailing `](/u)`. For example, `[x [y](z) https://e.com](/u)` links `https://e.com](/u)`. Marked already autolinks that same text when it appears outside any link.
